result.rationale: The diff shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` replacing the prior `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full safeParse envelope (`refreshTokenResponse` with `.success`/`.data`), so the envelope object is written via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` instead of the parsed credential data. On next instantiation the credential.key would no longer match googleCredentialSchema, breaking refresh and likely calendar access.

judged_text: Google Calendar writes the zod safeParse envelope returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse ({ success, data }) directly into credential.key instead of the parsed credentials (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97), so on the next load googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) throws, the integration is dead, and the user must re-authenticate — this hits every Google Calendar user on first access-token expiry in the default configuration

adjudication.rationale: In googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the code now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and persists `{ key }` via prisma. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the Zod `safeParse` result envelope (`{ success, data, ... }`), not `data` itself. Other call sites (e.g., office365calendar, zoomvideo) treat its return value as an envelope and access `.success`/`.data`. Persisting the envelope into `credential.key` would change the stored shape and can break later code expecting the credential JSON to match `googleCredentialSchema` (i.e., expecting actual credentials fields at the top level).
